course.title: Deep Learning, Fall 2024
course.instructor: Phillip Isola, Sara Beery, Jeremy Bernstein

coverage.note: Lectures 1-12. lecturesTotal counts the catalog's 24 recordings: 23 lectures (numbered 1-21, 23, 24; there is no lecture 22) plus a PyTorch tutorial.

license.summary: The course is published on MIT OpenCourseWare under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, and this repository (transcripts, slide transcriptions, slide images and wiki prose) is offered under the same licence. Third-party figures that OCW marks as excluded from its licence are described in prose only and never rendered into raw/images/.

figureAudit.note: All twelve transcribed decks were audited against the PDF by an independent reader. Lecture 1 (Sonnet transcription, Sonnet audit): six chart- and figure-heavy pages (21, 28, 51, 61, 63, 72), all agreeing, three small corrections applied; renders of slides 23, 45 and 70 also checked. Lecture 2 (Sonnet transcription, Sonnet audit): eight chart-, diagram- and number-heavy pages (10, 12, 14, 19, 51, 52, 79, 80) from cropped renders; seven agreed, slide 19 had two corrections, now applied; renders of slides 19 and 53 also checked. Lecture 3 (handwritten deck; Sonnet transcription, Opus audit): 19 equation-, diagram- and chart-heavy pages (5, 6, 10, 12-17, 27-33, 35, 38, 39) from 250-1200 dpi crops; every formula agreed; corrections applied on slides 6, 12, 27, 29, 30-33 (the layer symbol is a capital L) and 38 (values, and two series start points the first reading had invented), plus minor colour and arrow fixes; renders of slides 29 and 38 also checked. Lecture 4 (Sonnet transcription, Opus audit): 24 chart-, equation- and diagram-heavy pages (7, 8, 10, 18, 25, 31, 32, 37, 39-41, 48-52, 58-60, 62, 71, 77-79) from 600 dpi crops; every equation agreed; corrections on 13 pages, mostly counts (training points and peaks on slides 7, 8 and 10, nodes on 37 and 58, grid sizes on 59 and 60); it also found that slides 50-52 reuse slide 25's OCW-excluded clown fish image without a notice, so they are not rendered; renders of slides 42 and 74 also checked. Lecture 5 (Sonnet transcription, Opus audit): 27 graph-, chart- and equation-heavy pages (3, 5, 8-13, 15-20, 22, 23, 27, 28, 30, 35-37, 39-41, 43, 44) from 250-600 dpi crops, counting nodes, edges and bars from the PDF's vector data; every equation agreed and the flagged printed slips were confirmed, plus one more (slide 18's missing closing brace); corrections on 11 pages, mostly counts (nine red dots on slide 8, 16 edges on slide 9, eight curves on slide 41) and arrow ends (slides 16 and 43); renders of slides 36 and 41 also checked. Lecture 6 (Sonnet transcription, Opus audit): 30 chart-, diagram-, table- and equation-heavy pages (3, 8, 10, 11, 19, 25-28, 30-32, 34, 37-39, 44, 49-54, 56-60, 62, 63) from 150-600 dpi crops and vector data; every equation and every cell of slide 44's table agreed; corrections on 16 pages, mostly positions and counts (stems and arrow targets on slide 8, off-curve samples and spikes on 25-28, log axes and marker positions on 31-32, purple circles on 37 and 39); it also found that slide 62's photograph is lecture 4's excluded heron image, so slide 62 is not rendered; renders of slides 8 and 28 also checked. Lecture 7 (handwritten deck; Sonnet transcription, Opus audit): 24 pages (1, 4-7, 10-19, 22-26, 28-31) from 150-800 dpi crops, vector ink and the native rasters of slide 7's plots; every formula agreed and every flagged reading was settled (slide 11's lambda/2 and slide 18's ||g||_1 also against the recording); corrections on 15 pages, mostly colours, dot counts (slides 6 and 22) and arrow directions, plus slide 7's left plot (where width 32's minimum sits; the right branches are near-parallel) and slide 14's 'stray mark', which is the bracket's own top bar, not a transpose; renders of slides 22 and 24 also checked. Lecture 8 (Sonnet transcription, Opus audit): 33 diagram-, equation-, code- and photo-heavy pages (4, 5, 11, 13-17, 19, 21-24, 26, 28-31, 34-36, 38, 39, 41-44, 46, 47, 49, 51, 52, 54) from 150-600 dpi crops, vector data and embedded rasters; every equation agreed and slide 39's code character for character; corrections on 19 pages, mostly counts and arrow placement (ten birds on slide 4, ten circles on 13, eleven nodes with one pair unjoined on 24, seven and six circles and a 6 x 7 matrix in slide 35's conv row with its attn row's pink and orange arrows swapped, the decoder columns of slide 54 shifted one right so its first causal layer goes strictly forward); it settled every flagged reading (slide 31's frames carry no attention overlay in the PDF); renders of slides 35 and 54 also checked. Lecture 9 (Sonnet transcription, Opus audit): 34 figure-, chart-, table-, equation- and code-heavy pages (4, 7, 9, 10, 12-18, 20, 22-24, 27, 28, 30, 31, 34, 35, 38, 39, 43, 47, 50, 51, 54, 57, 58, 60, 61, 68, 71) from 60-600 dpi crops, native rasters and vector data; every equation, code line and table cell agreed, and the printed slips on slides 10, 12, 30 and 54 were confirmed; corrections on 13 pages, mostly counts and positions (six loss spikes on slides 4 and 57, 39 and 7 circles on slide 14, a 15 x 15 patch on slides 38-39, where slide 50's leader lines end), plus slide 30's spoon that is not there and its hidden tail fin, and slide 58's headings, which print 'Ll', 'Olayers', 'llayers' and '61ayers'; renders of slides 10 and 14 also checked. A same-model audit (lectures 1 and 2) catches misreadings caused by resolution but not ones the two readers share. Lecture 10 (Sonnet transcription, Opus audit): 44 figure-, diagram-, chart-, table- and equation-heavy pages (3, 5, 9-14, 16, 18, 19, 23-28, 31, 33, 34, 36-39, 41-45, 47, 49-53, 56, 58-62, 64, 65, 69) from 50-600 dpi renders, native rasters, vector data and the text layer; every equation and all 16 cells of slide 59's table agreed; corrections on 10 pages, two of them details not on the page (red arrows beside U on slide 26, an 'A' on slide 33's middle cell), the rest counts and positions (eight video frames and LVU near 17 on slide 64, three global rows and columns on slide 61, the reordered grid labels on slide 60, the full-size 'a' on slide 41); renders of slides 26 and 33 also checked. Lecture 11 (Sonnet transcription, Opus audit): 43 figure-, diagram-, chart-, table- and equation-heavy pages (3-5, 7-14, 16-21, 25, 26, 28, 31, 32, 35, 38-40, 42-49, 52, 53, 55, 57-61, 63) from 55-600 dpi renders, native rasters, vector data and the text layer, in two passes because a session limit stopped the first auditor after six pages; every equation and all 18 cells of slide 35's table agreed, and the charts on slides 43 and 61 were measured from their vector markers; corrections on 13 pages, all counts, positions and drawing order (three sheets and five dotted paths on slide 3, a second mapping picture in every row of slide 9, 108 patches on slide 19, 500 dots on slide 46, the channel slabs of slide 58's cubes); renders of slides 9 and 61 also checked. Lecture 12 (Sonnet transcription, Opus audit): 46 figure-, diagram-, chart-, equation- and photo-heavy pages (1, 6-8, 11-14, 17-25, 28-37, 39, 41-43, 48-55, 58-60, 64, 66-68) from 100-600 dpi renders, native rasters, vector data, the fonts and the text layer, in four passes because a session limit stopped the first two auditors after 15 and 10 pages; every equation agreed but slide 39's mutual-information bound, which prints the loss with no subscript; the stray marks in slides 28-30, 32 and 39's contrastive loss were settled as real glyphs whose size and position support the transcribed readings; slide 43's 306 and 108 encoders were counted marker by marker and the values of slides 48, 50-52 and 60 agree within half a point; corrections on 26 pages, three of them relations described that are not on the page (the caption colours of slides 18, 19 and 21, a changed circle on slide 36, a pointer on slide 52), the rest counts, positions and wording (slide 43's triangles and second row of markers, 57 tiles on slide 54, slide 24's badges, slide 31's wedge, slide 48's notice); slide 37's garbled labels were decoded by a consistent glyph substitution; renders of slides 35 and 50 also checked.

Lecture 5's slides 12, 15, 21 and 29 reuse the graph drawing of excluded slide 3 but are rendered: the only shared image object is a small node glyph, and slide 3's credit and notice sit under its Pinterest figure, not that graph. Lecture 9's slide 57 repeats slide 4's loss plot, sample grid and creature frame but not its chest X-ray, which is what slide 4's notice sits beside, so slide 57 is rendered. caveats: Covers lectures 1-12 of 24 only. The course map says which later lecture teaches a topic, but nothing here records what those lectures say.
Transcripts are OCW's human-made captions with a light copy-edit; every change is listed in the file header and the unedited text is in raw/transcripts/original/.
Lecture 1's deck labels later topics with 'Lecture N' banners that do not all match the recorded schedule (e.g. transformers 'Lecture 9', recorded as 8); wiki/course-map.md maps them.
Slides 45 and 70 of lecture 1 are animation frames clipped in OCW's PDF; their heat maps and batch matrices are not recoverable from the deck.
The lecture 1 deck's title slide reads '6.S898 Deep Learning, Fall 2022' - a reused deck, transcribed as printed.
Lecture 2's deck ends with a worked numerical backprop example (slides 72-80) that the recording does not reach; the wiki takes it from the slides alone.
Lecture 2's slide 79 misprints one multiplier (-0.1186 for -0.1869; its printed result uses the right value), and its weight-update slides use +eta with a negative learning rate; the wiki flags both.

Lecture 3's deck is handwritten (iPad notes); its PDF text layer is OCR noise and was not used. Everything was read from page images, and the equation-, diagram- and chart-heavy pages were audited by a different model.
Lecture 3's slide 30 prints KINKS_0 = 1 as the base case of its kink-counting bound; in the recording a student corrects it to 0 and the base case is left unresolved. The wiki reports both.
Lecture 3's slide 39 cites the Chinchilla paper as 'Hoffmann, Borgeau, Mensch et al (2020)'; it is transcribed as written.

Lecture 4's deck has 35 of 84 slides excluded from OCW's licence, including every figure built on the stork and heron photographs (segmentation, feature maps, receptive fields, encoder-decoder, U-net, ResNet); those exist here as prose descriptions only.

Lecture 4's slide 40 prints x_out[C, :] where its 0-based indexing means C - 1, and slide 39 leaves unclear whether the bias is inside the channel sum; the lecturer calls slide 25's vertical-edge filter 'horizontal edges'. The wiki flags all three.

Lecture 5's deck has 14 of 47 slides excluded from OCW's licence (the application examples, J. Leskovec's tree-view illustrations, the two example architectures, the positional-encoding results); those exist here as prose descriptions only.

Lecture 5's slide 41 plots eight training-accuracy curves but labels only three groups with arrows (sum with an MLP, sum with linear+ReLU, mean/max); per-curve values are read approximately from the plot.

Lecture 5's slides print small slips, transcribed as written and flagged: slide 18's max aggregation lacks its closing brace, slides 40-41 drop the opening bracket after g_1, slide 30's first coefficient c^{vu} carries no r, and slide 39's h^(t) is unbolded with no node subscript.

Lecture 6's deck has 8 of 66 slides excluded from OCW's licence (the Paul the octopus article, the pix2pix and edges2cats figures, all four Belkin et al. double-descent figures, and the NeRF and polypharmacy figures); those exist here as prose descriptions only, and slide 62 is not rendered because its photograph is lecture 4's excluded heron image.

Lecture 6's slides 10-11 print n = 30, m = 10 for a 30-fruit vocabulary and 10-fruit lists (the reverse of slide 9's definitions), and slide 10's s = 100 trillion matches neither 10^30 nor 30^10; the wiki reports the numbers without resolving them.
Lecture 6's slides 41 and 43 call the number of dichotomies the 'VC dimension'; the wiki follows the slides, with one note marked as outside the course material that textbook usage differs.

Lecture 7's deck is handwritten (iPad notes), like lecture 3's; its text layer is OCR noise and was not used except for OCW's typed notices. 3 of its 32 slides (7, 25, 26) carry Keller Jordan's plots, which OCW excludes from its licence; they exist here as prose descriptions only, including slides 25 and 26's handwritten width claim and depth recipe.

Lecture 7's slides print small slips, transcribed as written and flagged: slide 11's boxed Newton step drops the lambda of the line above it, slides 13-15 write the Gauss-Newton product with no transpose, slide 19 says 'right had side' and prints the dual formulation of steepest descent with no minus sign (problem set 2's version has one).

In lecture 7's recording the lecturer says (1 + x/L^2)^L tends to 0; the wiki reports it with one note marked as outside the course material that the limit is 1. He also says depth increases 'as I go down' the curves of slide 7's depth plot, the reverse of the plot; the wiki gives both.

Lecture 8's deck has 7 of 55 slides excluded from OCW's licence (Fredo Durand's bird photograph on slides 4 and 6-8, the DINO attention maps, the ScaleMAE figure, and the 'Attention Is All You Need' figure); those exist here as prose descriptions only. Its outline slide is headed '9. Transformers' although the title slide and recording are lecture 8.

Lecture 8's slide 29 prints key-query scores (1, 0.2, 0.9, 0.1) that do not match its attention weights (0.1, 0.2, 1, 0.1), which do not sum to 1; the lecturer calls the first score a typo for 0.1. Its slide 39 pseudocode reuses K for the patch size and the key matrix and divides by sqrt(d) outside the softmax, where slide 34 divides inside; slide 34 scales by sqrt(m) while its diagram labels the dimension M. The wiki reports each as printed.

In lecture 8's recording the lecturer says attention is 'permutation invariant' where slide 41 says equivariant, and that layer norm divides 'by the variance' where slide 38 divides by its square root; the wiki gives both.

Lecture 9's deck has 21 of 72 slides excluded from OCW's licence (the chest X-ray, the coffee-cup loading example, the augmentation photographs, the domain-randomization images and OpenAI's robot-hand results, the Stable Diffusion and AlphaFold screenshots, every colorization photograph, a facade-generation grid, and the Weights & Biases, spice-rack and Scale ML screenshots); those exist here as prose descriptions only.

Lecture 9's recording runs out of time after the model section: most of the optimization, evaluation, debugging and compute slides (48-71) are never spoken, and the wiki takes them from the slides alone.

In lecture 9's recording the lecturer describes slide 4's DeGrave, Janizek and Lee example as a breast-cancer (benign or malignant) classifier; the slide shows a chest X-ray and names no disease. The wiki gives both, with one note marked as outside the course material that the cited paper concerns COVID-19 detection from chest radiographs.

Lecture 9's slides print small slips, transcribed as written and flagged: slide 10's layernorm mean carries 1/k in front of a sum over k, slide 30's argmin formula has unbalanced parentheses, and slide 70 writes torch.cudnn.benchmark (the wiki adds one note marked as outside the course material that PyTorch's flag is torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark).

Lecture 10's deck has 20 of 69 slides excluded from OCW's licence (the classroom video frame, the video strip, audio waveform, space-time cube and its slices, the photographs of the lecturer's cat Frank, which OCW marks '© source unknown', and the Reformer and Longformer figures); those exist here as prose descriptions only. Its outline slides are headed '11. Memory and sequence modeling' (slides 2 and 67) and '9. Memory and sequence modeling' (slide 68) although the title slide and recording are lecture 10.

Lecture 10's LSTM slides (33-39) are derived from Chris Olah's blog post and use its plain notation (x_t, h_t, C_t), not the bold notation of the rest of the deck; the wiki follows each slide's notation.

In lecture 10's recording the lecturer calls the hidden-to-hidden weights 'v' where slide 23 has W, calls the powers of W 'quadratic' before calling them exponential, says 'maximizing cross-entropy' where slide 50 says minimize, and describes byte pairs as two-character pairs, about 26 times 26 of them (lecture 8 has a byte pair for 'I-N-G'); the transcript marks the first three and the wiki gives each beside the slide.

Lecture 11's deck has 22 of 65 slides excluded from OCW's licence (the car, fish and bird photographs used throughout, Serre's visual-cortex diagram, Zeiler and Fergus's patch mosaics, the colorization photographs, the conv5 stimulus grid and Yann LeCun's cake slide); those exist here as prose descriptions only, and slide 13 is not rendered because its CLIP figure is lecture 1's excluded slide 73 figure. Its outline slide is headed '12. Representation Learning I' although the title slide and recording are lecture 11.

Lecture 11's slide 9 prints the softmax with a minus sign in the exponent, e^{-tau x}, and its wiring-graph node without the tau; slide 60 cites the masked-autoencoder paper ([He, Chen, Xie, et al. 2021]) for BERT; slides 25-28 print 'Neural' where 'Neutral' is meant. The slide file transcribes each as printed, and the wiki gives slide 9's formula as printed.

In lecture 11's recording the lecturer works the linear-autoencoder-equals-PCA derivation from equations that are not in the OCW deck (slide 41 prints only the conclusion); the wiki gives the argument in his words without reconstructing the equations. He calls k-means' optimizer expectation maximization where slide 48 says block coordinate descent, and assigns the coloured-shapes experiments to 'p set 3' where OCW has them in Homework 4; the wiki gives both.

Lecture 12's deck has 37 of 70 slides excluded from OCW's licence (nearly every photograph, Wang and Isola's hypersphere and alignment figures, the CIFAR-10 feature heat maps, the augmentation chart, Chuang et al.'s and Khosla et al.'s figures, and the whole iNaturalist case study, slides 54-68); those exist here as prose descriptions only. 35 of the 37 notices are drawn as vector glyph outlines that the PDF text layer does not contain; the excluded set was taken from the vision-read slide file and confirmed by a scan of the vector paths.

In lecture 12's recording the lecturer defines the alignment and uniformity metrics and splits the contrastive loss into two terms as the number of negatives goes to infinity, without a slide in the OCW deck (about 47:38-50:49); the wiki gives both in her words and reconstructs no formula. She puts the crop-only augmentation loss at '15% almost' where slide 48's chart shows about 27 points for SimCLR, and the batch-size gap early in training at 'close to 10%' where slide 51 shows about 7 points; the wiki gives both.

Lecture 12's slides 28-30, 32 and 39 print the transpose, temperature, 'distributed as' and summation signs of the contrastive loss as stray marks, and slide 39 a breve for the script L and no subscript on the loss in its mutual-information bound; the wiki gives the reading the layout supports. The garbled anchor and heading of slide 37 were decoded by a consistent glyph substitution.
